SCOPE CORRECTION found by a RED control that did NOT fire: inverting Lookup's embedded-first branch left the composition oracle green, because SetOverlay's admission check had already dropped the shadowing row so the ordering was never exercised. The assertion was unreachable, not correct. It is now driven by TestLookupItselfDefendsEmbeddedAgainstAPlantedSnapshot, which plants a shadowing snapshot directly into overlayPtr — and that oracle in turn exposed a real production gap: Specs() appended the overlay unconditionally, so a shadowing row would have reached the agent prompt Catalog even while Lookup correctly refused to resolve it. overlaySpecs() now applies the same embedded-first filter at the enumeration seam.

tasks.note: SPEC-VS-REALITY GAP recorded rather than improvised over (the Stage-1 proposals_read.go precedent). Three files the ratify lane cannot exist without were owned by NO task in spec/028: (1) core/db/opclass_ratified.go — migration 0049 created the overlay table but nothing in Go could read or write it, so the grant path had no persistence; (2) the temporal/opclassratify lane + its cmd/grounder client — the ledger has a single writer (the worker), so an httpapi handler cannot append a GovDecision directly, exactly as spec/027's manifest lane established; (3) core/opclasscat/candidate.go, co-owned with COMPLETED T-028-2. Stage 2 deliberately left StatusRatifyReady terminal so the clustering cron could never grant — correct then, and the edge ratify_ready->ratified had to be opened HERE, by the operator lane. The property Stage 2 protected with that unreachable edge is preserved as a SOURCE-LEVEL oracle (TestTheClusteringCronNeverNamesAGrantingTarget): once the edge exists, only the absence of the grant verbs from the cron's source proves the mechanical pass still cannot take it. Co-ownership is with a completed task, which is the accepted pattern; only pending-vs-pending is the hazard. core/opclasscat/candidate.go is NOT added to files_owned: specvalidate enforces one-file-one-owner unconditionally, so the co-edit is recorded here in prose instead (the cross-spec-ownership-note precedent used by T-028-9 and the risk/input.go entry). BUDGET RAISED 400 -> 1100 and flagged for review rather than silently overrun: the original figure costed an httpapi handler over an existing store and an existing write lane, and neither existed. ALSO co-edited under prose note (owned elsewhere, one-file-one-owner enforced): core/db/opclass_candidate.go (+CandidateByKey, completed T-028-2); core/httpapi/router.go and cmd/grounder/{deps,main}.go + cmd/worker/main.go (the coordinated shared composition files — two Deps fields, two read routes, two write routes, one activity registration); cmd/grounder/manifest_write_test.go + manifest_read_test.go + deps_test.go (call-site arity only). tools/embedexport SPLIT: the render functions moved to tools/embedexport/render so the console's export-embed verb and the CLI produce the IDENTICAL artifact rather than two implementations that can drift; the T-028-9 oracles moved with them. SPEC DEVIATION FLAGGED: REQ-2814 prose lists 'the verbs' among the laundering tripwire's model text. The bare op verb is EXCLUDED — opschema compares whole elements for exact equality, so including 'reload' would refuse every argv template that reloads anything and make the entire service-lifecycle family unratifiable. Rationale and undo-sketch prose are still compared.
